label: Animated bookmark portrait
summary: An animated portrait picture of a bookmark character, played with a chosen animation group.
details: The game gives no description and no return type that names anything. Vanilla's animation test window uses it as the picture of a portrait, passing a bookmark key, the selected animation group, an environment name, a camera name and the size of the widget.

fields.name: arguments
fields.text: Five values in this order: bookmark key, animation group, environment, camera, and the widget's screen size (vanilla uses PdxGetWidgetScreenSize of the widget).
fields.values: three text keys, an animation group and a size

label: Animation tooltip
summary: Text for a tooltip about an animation, built from a widget and a character.
details: The game gives no description; its return type is text. Vanilla uses it once, in the shared tooltip GUI file, passing the widget itself and a character. Going by its name, it produces tooltip text about an animation.

fields.name: widget, character
fields.text: The widget showing the tooltip and the character.

label: Archery contest aptitude
summary: The shown character's aptitude (how suited they are) for the archery contest type.
details: A shortcut for GetContestAptitude with the archery aptitude script value. The game's documentation says it works on the character in the current window. Vanilla uses it in the tournament widget to drive a segmented progress bar.

label: Artifact type
summary: The artifact type with the given key.

label: Artifact visual type
summary: The artifact visual type (the look of an artifact) with the given key.

label: Autosave name
summary: The name under which the game will write its autosave.
details: Vanilla shows it in the frontend texts "Save the game as ..." and "The game will be saved as ...". Its return type is text.

label: B of a decimal vector
summary: The B part of a four-value decimal vector (a CVector4f).
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. It returns a decimal number and takes one argument that the game does not describe. The reading of B and of the argument comes from the name only.

fields.name: argument
fields.text: One value; the game does not say what it is.

label: B of an integer vector
summary: The B part of a four-value whole-number vector (a CVector4i).
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. It returns a whole number and takes one argument that the game does not describe. The reading comes from the name only.

fields.name: argument
fields.text: One value; the game does not say what it is.

label: Bookmark
summary: The bookmark with the given key.
details: Vanilla also uses it with no key, after a bookmark character, to get that character's bookmark in the frontend.

label: Bookmark group
summary: The bookmark group with the given key.

label: Bookmark portrait
summary: The bookmark portrait with the given key.
details: Vanilla's credits window uses it with a credit portrait entry and then asks the result for the actual picture.

label: Build version
summary: Text describing the game's build version.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the main HUD.

label: Build version, click to copy
summary: Text describing the game's build version, the variant whose name mentions click to copy.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip on the loading screen. Going by its name, it adds a click-to-copy hint to the build version text.

label: Building
summary: The building type with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name, for example to name a building in a requirement text.

label: Can go to frontend
summary: Whether the player may go back to the main menu in a multiplayer game.
details: The game's documentation labels it a multiplayer GUI check. It returns yes or no.

label: Why not to frontend
summary: The message that says why going back to the main menu is not possible.
details: The game's documentation labels it a multiplayer GUI message for the case where going back is not possible; it returns text.

label: Casus belli type
summary: The casus belli type (the justification for a war) with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for its name.

label: Catalyst type
summary: The situation catalyst type with the given key, or the catalyst type of an entry in a catalyst history.
details: Vanilla uses it after a catalyst history entry to ask for the name.

label: Challenge character
summary: The challenge character with the given key.
details: Vanilla uses it on the main frontend view.

label: 1v1 contest opponent
summary: The opponent character of a one-on-one contest round, read from a variable of the shown character named by the round.
details: The documented macro text is Character.MakeScope.GetVariable( RoundName ).Char, which reads a character stored in a variable. The documented description sentence is the same as for GetCharacterContest1v1OpponentPtV and does not fit; vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: RoundName
fields.text: Name of the variable that holds the round's opponent.

label: 1v1 contest PtV
summary: The progress-to-victory value (PTV) tied to a one-on-one contest round's opponent.
details: The game's documentation describes it as the player's PTV against their 1v1 opponent. Its macro text is GetTargetCharacterPtV applied to GetCharacterContest1v1Opponent, which suggests it is the opponent's value, so doc description and macro do not clearly agree. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: RoundName
fields.text: Name of the round (the variable that holds the opponent).

label: Character interaction
summary: The character interaction with the given key.
details: Vanilla uses it on the notification windows of interactions, then asks whether the effects should be shown.

label: Interaction category
summary: The character interaction category with the given key.
details: Vanilla uses it in the interaction menu to read the category's colour.

label: Interaction category by number
summary: The character interaction category at the given position in the list.
details: The game gives no description; the game's documentation lists it as a promoted function returning an interaction category, and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name, it picks a category by its position instead of its key.

label: Memory type
summary: The character memory type with the given key.
details: The game lists its return type as a null type, so what it hands back is unclear.

label: Character PtV
summary: The shown character's PTV, the value of their variable progress_to_victory.
details: The documented macro text is Character.MakeScope.Var( 'progress_to_victory' ).GetValue. The return type is not given and vanilla does not use it.

label: Emblem categories
summary: The categories of emblem textures in the coat of arms designer.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list in the coat of arms designer.

label: Coloured value text
summary: Text for a value, probably written in a colour.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. It takes three values and returns text; going by its name it colours a value, but what each argument means is not known.

fields.name: arguments
fields.text: Three values; their roles are not documented.

label: Command description
summary: The description text of a game command.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla passes it a command such as abandoning the ruler objective, for the tooltip of a button, and uses it in a legend tooltip too.

fields.name: command
fields.text: The game command whose description is wanted.
fields.values: a GUI command such as the ones vanilla passes for the ruler objective buttons

label: Confederation type
summary: The confederation type with the given key.

label: Connection arrow type
summary: The connection arrow type with the given key.
details: The game lists its return type as a null type, so what it hands back is unclear.

label: Contest aptitude
summary: The shown character's aptitude for a contest, read from a named script value.
details: The game's documentation says it gets the script value of the character in the current window. The argument is the name of that script value (the archery shortcut passes 'contest_type_aptitude_archery').

fields.name: script value
fields.text: Name of the script value that measures the aptitude.

label: Cost text
summary: The cost of something written out as text.
details: The game gives no description; it returns text. Vanilla uses it after a court type setting, after a men-at-arms type (with the player as the argument) for "Creation cost: ...", and in a domicile text.

fields.name: payer
fields.text: Who the cost is for; vanilla passes the player for men-at-arms types and nothing for a court type setting.

label: Cost value
summary: The cost of something as a number.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name and result type (a fixed-point number), it is the number form of the cost text. Its two arguments are not documented.

fields.name: arguments
fields.text: Two values; their roles are not documented.

label: Council position type
summary: The council position type with the given key, or the position type of a window about a possible councillor.
details: Vanilla uses it on the potential councillor window.

label: Council task type
summary: The council task type with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name, for example the conversion task in domicile building texts.

label: Court amenities setting
summary: The court amenities setting with the given key.

label: Grandeur gap modifier
summary: The modifier that goes with a given difference between the court's grandeur level and the expected level.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla gives it the difference from the court grandeur data in the court amenities window.

fields.name: difference
fields.text: The gap between the court's level and the expected level.

label: Grandeur level modifier
summary: The modifier that goes with a court grandeur level.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla gives it the current level and asks for the name, in the royal court and grandeur windows.

label: Court position task
summary: The court position task type with the given key.

label: Court position type
summary: The court position type with the given key.
details: Very common in vanilla texts, which write the key in quotes and ask for the name, for example to say that a building unlocks a court position.

label: Court scene slot position
summary: The on-screen position of an inventory slot in the court scene.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla uses it in the royal court window with the parent widget and an inventory slot, to set where a widget goes.

fields.name: widget, slot
fields.text: A widget and the inventory slot.

label: Court type
summary: The court type with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name, for example to list court types. The 'Custom('GetCourtType')' lines in the input are a different thing, a custom text of that name.

label: Credit portraits
summary: The credit portraits of one side of the credits window.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla calls it with 'left' and 'right' as the data source of the credits lists.

label: Culture by key
summary: The culture with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key to name a culture or to get its collective noun.

label: Culture era type
summary: The culture era type with the given key, or the era of an innovation.
details: Vanilla uses it after a culture innovation type in the culture window to read the era's frame.

label: Innovation type
summary: The cultural innovation type with the given key.

label: Culture pillar
summary: The culture pillar with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name.

label: Culture template
summary: The culture template with the given key.

label: Culture tradition
summary: The cultural tradition with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name, for example "their culture has the ... tradition".

label: Current date
summary: The game's current date.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla's ledger reads its year to compare with an artifact's age and with culture creation years, and the great project planning window compares it with an expected end date.

label: Date text with sync info
summary: The current date as text, with information about multiplayer synchronisation.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name, it is the date text plus sync information.

label: Date plus offset
summary: Text for the date that lies a given time from now.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla texts feed it the time remaining of a variable and use it for "cannot be done until ..." cooldown messages.

fields.name: time
fields.values: a time span, such as the remaining time of a variable

label: Date plus offset, long
summary: Text for the date a given time from now, probably in a long form.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name, it is the long-form twin of GetCurrentDateWithDiff.

label: Date plus offset, short
summary: Text for the date a given time from now, probably in a short form.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name, it is the short-form twin of GetCurrentDateWithDiff.

label: Current FPS
summary: The current frames per second of the game, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it as "FPS: ..." and in a low-FPS warning.

label: Game speed
summary: The current game speed, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla's HUD uses it to pick the frame of the speed icon.

label: Game speed text
summary: The current game speed written as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the game speed tooltip.

label: Own house unity stage text
summary: Text describing the house unity stage of the local player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text of the house unity level game concept.

label: Current loading screen
summary: The loading screen being shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the frontend loading screen.

label: Current map mode
summary: Going by its name, the map mode currently shown.
details: Its only line in vanilla is commented out: in the ledger window it would save the current map mode's key under the name `mapmode_before_ledger` (marked as a TODO). The game documents nothing more.

label: List size
summary: How many entries a list (data model) has.
details: The game gives no description and returns a whole number. The name appears about 520 times in vanilla texts, for example inside a subtraction that counts the entries of an activity guest list.

fields.name: list
fields.text: The list whose entries are counted.
fields.values: a list from the GUI, such as an activity window's guest list

label: Decision
summary: The decision with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a quoted key and ask for the name, for example "use the ... decision".

label: Decision group
summary: The decision group type with the given key.

label: Decision by key
summary: The decision with the given key.
details: The game gives no description. It is used a lot in vanilla texts in the same way as GetDecision, with a quoted key and a name request.

label: Decisions of a character
summary: A list of decisions for the given character.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla passes it the player and uses it as the data source of a list in the shared tooltip file. Going by its name, it lists the decisions of that character.

label: Slow-down tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the button that slows the game down.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name, it is the text for the decrease-speed control.

label: Deepest tooltip info
summary: The tooltip information (a TooltipInfo) of the deepest level, going by its name.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla uses it as a data context for widgets, with a comment that tooltip info does not pass down into grid box items.

label: Default server name
summary: The default name offered for a multiplayer server.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the multiplayer game setup.

label: Game define
summary: The value of a named setting from the game's defines files.
details: The game gives no description. Vanilla texts call it with a group name and a setting name (such as 'NCharacter' or 'NCharacterOpinion') and show the value, in one case as a percentage.

fields.name: group
fields.values: a quoted text, e.g. a character group

label: Game define by position
summary: One entry of a list-valued define.
details: The game gives no description and vanilla does not use it. Going by its name and three arguments, it likely takes the group, the name and the position of the entry.
